paragraphs: Scope and boundaries: this page covers only the tasks and conditions of O*NET 41-9012.00 (Models), excluding responsibilities of adjacent roles such as photography, styling, makeup, and fashion design. Organizers and professionals bear responsibility for equipment, locations, and safety on shoots.

How to assess: first check through an entirely fictional, low-cost shoot or life drawing assignment whether you can consistently present as requested, accept repeated adjustments, and proactively verify contracts and material usage scope. Interest and personality assessments cannot replace these observations.

Who it suits: people willing to present their own image before cameras and face external evaluation over time, complete work with irregular schedules, and check contracts and permissions clause by clause. Note: if appearance judgments, income fluctuations, or upfront payment pressure are difficult to tolerate, first compare adjacent fields such as acting, imaging, and styling.

Note: the following are editorially designed paper exercises without real clients, brands, or locations. They do not constitute professional practice, likeness, or work permission. Judgments involving health, contracts, or immigration status require professionals and local rules.

Models (O*NET 41-9012.00) display clothing or accessories to prospective buyers at fashion shows, private showings, or retail settings. They may also pose for magazine or advertising shoots or serve as subjects for painting, sculpture, and other art. Their core output is presenting their own image on camera or on stage.

entries: Booking and preparation: obtain pay, date, time, and term information from agents or clients, prepare portfolios and comp cards, and prepare styling and posture according to shoot or runway requirements.
Presentation and collaboration: pose or walk the runway as directed, collaborate with photographers, stylists, makeup artists, directors, and clients, and complete shoots or performances on schedule.
Records and confirmation: record pay and hours on vouchers, report completion to agencies and obtain future bookings, and verify material usage scope and settlement.

paragraphs: Working arrangements: primarily paid by project, day, or class session, often working with agencies or direct clients. Requires managing schedules, styling preparation, and material authorization records.

Work context: 85% of O*NET respondents work indoors in controlled environments daily, 78% have continual contact with others, 45% have irregular schedules, 31% have seasonal schedules, and all respondents work fewer than 40 hours per week.

Preparation and training: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone 1–2, generally requiring a high school diploma or equivalent. Runway walking, camera presentation, and posture management are largely developed through practice and training.
Capabilities and working methods: requires posture and camera presentation skills, adaptability to styling and lighting changes, and consistent cooperation during long waits and repeated shoots.

Research inputs: official O*NET 41-9012.00 descriptions, tasks, work context, interest code (ARE), and Job Zone 1–2, plus BLS 2025 wages and 2024—2034 employment projections displayed by O*NET (national scope for this occupation).

Income and employment level: U.S. 2025 median hourly wage 23.30 USD (approximately 48,470 USD annually); 10th and 90th percentiles 16.44 and 63.21 USD respectively. Approximately 6,700 employed in 2024; 2024—2034 employment projected to show little or no change, with approximately 1,200 annual openings including replacement needs. These statistics exclude self-employed and project-based models.

Conclusion: models' core output is presenting their own image on camera or on stage. Actors focus on character performance, dancers on choreographed movement, fashion designers on clothing design, photographers on image capture, and theatrical makeup artists on makeup and hair execution. Adjacent relationships support comparisons only, not automatic transfers or mutual recognition of qualifications.

Comparisons use the official O*NET 41-9012.00 description and tasks and related O*NET profiles: actors 27-2011.00, dancers 27-2031.00, fashion designers 27-1022.00, photographers 27-4021.00, and theatrical makeup artists 39-5091.00. This is an editorial synthesis, not job recommendations.

entries: RIASEC interest signals: preferences for visual presentation, physical expression, and public display correspond to O*NET interest code ARE (Artistic 99, Realistic 67, Enterprising 45). Interests describe activity preferences only.
Big Five personality signals: no evidence establishes that a particular personality combination better suits this occupation; use for self-exploration only.
MBTI signals: not for determining fit or qualifications; check performance in real shoots.
Enneagram signals: a general self-exploration tool with no evidenced link to fit for this occupation.
O*NET items failing to meet display thresholds do not mean cognitive ability is irrelevant. This page has not obtained predictive research linking cognitive tests to modeling performance.
Emotional intelligence signals: remaining steady during long waits and repeated adjustments is observable behavior, not a hiring standard.

paragraphs: Conclusion: assess fit through real task performance—consistent attendance, accepting repeated adjustments, and proactively verifying contracts and material usage scope. Assessment results are not qualification or hiring standards.
Evidence level: interests and work styles for this occupation come from official O*NET profiles. Other assessment tools are general psychological measures for self-exploration only.

Boundaries: this page lists common work pressures and risks only, not medical, legal, or safety advice. Questions involving health, contracts, likeness, and minors' working conditions require professionals and local rules.

The main pressures to assess in advance are weight and appearance judgments, project-based income fluctuations, and unclear likeness and material usage scope. Their relative importance differs across runway, editorial and advertising, e-commerce imagery, and art modeling.

Evidence scope: work context percentages come from the O*NET Work Context survey (United States); scam signals from the U.S. FTC; peer-reviewed body pressure studies use limited populations; French and other national rules apply only in their jurisdictions.
Runway, editorial, and advertising models, and young models entering the field
May affect health and career sustainability and whether bookings continue. Relevant requirements should rely on written conditions and professional medical judgment.

Entry stage: can present as requested throughout a low-cost shoot or art modeling assignment and truthfully report personal feelings and difficulties.
Entry practice
Consistent booking stage: can reliably attend despite irregular schedules, present different styles as directed, and proactively verify work orders and pay.

Independent responsibility stage: can adjust presentation with art direction and styling teams on site and independently confirm materials and permissions.
Independent responsibility
Long-term collaboration stage: can undertake ongoing brand projects, participate in creative communication, and make clear requests about permissions, pay, and compliance conditions.

ai_impact_table.responsibility_intro: The following sequence is an editorial verification path explaining which steps people should control when AI is involved, not an official mandatory procedure.

responsibility_steps.说明: Confirm shoot or event goals, required poses and accessories, and final images or live effects to deliver.
Specify image usage geography, duration, media, and whether generative modifications or digital replicas are permitted in the contract.
After shooting, verify that final images accurately represent clothing, colors, and styles to avoid misleading presentation.
When materials are reused or modified, verify that usage remains within original permissions and retain communication and permission records.
Retain work orders, permissions, and payment records. Refer out-of-scope use or likeness disputes to agents, clients, and local legal channels.

risk_rows.为什么重要: Unchecked generated images may misrepresent clothing, colors, or body shapes, affecting brand and consumer judgments
risk_rows.控制方式: The individual or project lead must verify final images and generated content before external use
risk_rows.风险: Using tool outputs directly as finished products

risk_rows.为什么重要: One authorized material may be expanded into media, regions, or periods not agreed upon
risk_rows.控制方式: Specify usage scope, duration, and geography in contracts and retain permission and communication records
risk_rows.风险: Likeness and materials reused beyond scope

risk_rows.为什么重要: Once body scans and facial data are collected, they may be reused without consent
risk_rows.控制方式: Verify collection purposes and retention periods; avoid providing biometric data unrelated to the current work
risk_rows.风险: Collection of data and body information

risk_rows.为什么重要: Digital replicas may bypass the individual's decisions on appearances and compensation
risk_rows.控制方式: Verify digital replica usage scenarios, duration, fees, and refusal or withdrawal conditions. Rights depend on contracts and local law.
risk_rows.风险: Using a 'digital replica' instead of the individual's attendance

risk_rows.为什么重要: Treating tool demonstrations or promotional cases as industry trends misleads career and income expectations
risk_rows.控制方式: Base judgments on official statistics and research; do not trust promises of 'guaranteed bookings'

ai_impact_table.transition: When moving from modeling to an adjacent occupation, first compare transferable capabilities in camera presentation, posture management, and collaborative shoots, then address the target field's specific knowledge, tools, and qualification requirements. Adjacent relationships do not imply automatic transfers or mutual recognition of qualifications.

career_path_block.direct_answer: Entry generally begins with portfolios and auditions. First check actual interests through a low-cost shoot or art modeling experience, then prepare portfolios and comp cards and apply through legitimate agencies or direct clients. Selection mainly considers presentation capability, on-site cooperation, and availability rather than a single appearance standard. Verify any agency requiring upfront fees or promising guaranteed bookings first.

risks.mitigation: Individuals and medical professionals determine health boundaries; do not trade extreme weight loss for work. Request written explanations of verbal demands making weight loss a hiring condition. France and some other countries require medical certificates for modeling practice; other countries have different rules. Verify local requirements separately.
risks.scenario: Projects making weight loss or appearance changes booking conditions
risks.title: Weight and appearance pressure

risks.affected_roles: Job seekers and guardians, especially people approached by 'scouts' online or on the street
risks.consequence: The other party requests upfront shooting, course, or 'placement' fees and promises work or high earnings
risks.mitigation: Legitimate agencies charge commissions after you obtain work and do not require advance payment for opportunities. Before signing, verify credentials and licenses where required, request contracts and commission rates, and check complaint records through public channels.
risks.scenario: Fees charged for 'image building' or 'guaranteed bookings'
risks.title: Fake recruitment and upfront payment scams

risks.affected_roles: Models booked through agencies, especially first-time commercial shoots
risks.consequence: Agents sign contracts without the individual seeing terms, and materials are used in unagreed media, regions, or periods
risks.mitigation: Request contract copies before signing, specify material usage scope, duration, geography, and whether generative modifications are allowed, and retain communication and permission records. For out-of-scope use, communicate through agents and clients and seek local legal channels.
risks.scenario: The individual cannot see the contract or permission scope is excessively broad
risks.title: Unclear contracts and likeness permissions

risks.affected_roles: Models involved in commercial shoots and e-commerce imagery, and people who have provided body scans
risks.consequence: Images or scan data collected during one shoot are used to generate new images or digital replicas beyond the original agreement
risks.mitigation: Verify scan and facial data purposes, retention periods, reuse, compensation, and withdrawal conditions, retaining contract records. Refusal and withdrawal rights depend on local law and contracts.
risks.scenario: Likeness or body data used for generated content
risks.title: Digital replica and generative AI usage boundaries

risks.affected_roles: Self-employed or project-paid models, especially those relying on bookings
risks.consequence: Irregular or seasonal schedules may create income gaps. Verify hours, pay methods, and cost allocation per project; do not assume all costs are out of pocket.
risks.mitigation: Calculate hourly pay and out-of-pocket costs per project, retain work orders and payment records, diversify clients, and reserve cash flow for quieter periods. U.S. wage figures on this page cover paid employees, excluding self-employment, and cannot directly establish individual income.
risks.scenario: Income fluctuations from project work and self-employment
risks.title: Unstable income and schedules

risks.affected_roles: Models at runway shows, trade shows, and consecutive shoots
risks.consequence: Prolonged standing or bending, frequent rapid clothing changes, and long waits in bright light or cold settings
risks.mitigation: Arrange breaks and changing procedures around work pacing and confirm changing facilities, warmth, and lighting beforehand. Stop work and seek medical care for persistent pain or discomfort; do not treat injury as an occupational price.
risks.scenario: Prolonged standing, bending, and frequent clothing changes
risks.title: Physical strain and work pacing

components.definition_block: Models correspond to O*NET 41-9012.00: they display clothing or accessories to prospective buyers at fashion shows, private showings, or retail settings, may pose for magazine or advertising shoots, or serve as subjects for painting, sculpture, and other art. Their core output is presenting their own image on camera or on stage, accompanied by auditions, work orders, portfolios, and material permission management. This page excludes responsibilities of adjacent roles such as photography, styling, makeup, and fashion design.

fermat_decision_card.summary: If you are willing to present your own image over time to cameras and external judgments and verify contracts and material usage scope despite irregular schedules, this direction warrants a low-cost trial. If appearance judgments and income fluctuations are difficult to tolerate, first compare adjacent fields such as acting, imaging, and styling.

hero.quick_answer: Models present clothing, accessories, products, or characters using their own image on camera or on stage according to client and production team requirements. Work centers on projects and agency bookings; first verify contracts, pay, likeness usage scope, and safety conditions.

Interest and personality tools help design trials only and do not determine qualifications, hiring, or capability.

directions.fit_signals: If playing other characters on camera through speech and emotional expression interests you more than presenting your own image, try an acting workshop first.
directions.watchouts: Actors require long-term acting training and face competition for roles. Their presentation logic differs from this occupation and is not directly interchangeable.

directions.fit_signals: If you prefer physical movement as your core expression, try a dance class to assess training intensity and physical conditions.
directions.watchouts: Dancers need systematic dance training and the ability to withstand long-term physical demands; their career paths differ substantially from this occupation.

directions.fit_signals: If garment construction, fabrics, and collection design interest you more, start with basic patternmaking or design courses.
directions.watchouts: Design requires patternmaking, fabric, and process knowledge, differing from shoot presentation capabilities.

directions.fit_signals: If you prefer controlling equipment, lighting, and image postproduction, start with a portrait photography project.
directions.watchouts: Photography requires equipment, lighting, and postproduction skills and bears technical responsibilities on shoots.

directions.fit_signals: If makeup, hair techniques, and character creation interest you more, start with a performance makeup internship.
directions.watchouts: Makeup and styling execution are adjacent roles with different capability and tool requirements.

directions.fit_signals: If you prefer product explanation and live promotion, first participate in a mall or trade show promotional event.
directions.watchouts: Promotion roles center on product explanation and sales support, differing from image presentation work.

personality_fit_block.heading: Modeling fit signals and exploration tools

questions.answer: Appearance requirements vary substantially across runway, advertising, e-commerce, and art modeling markets. This page sets no uniform threshold. Understand actual target market requirements before deciding whether the investment is worthwhile.
questions.question: Does failing a particular height or appearance standard rule out modeling?

questions.answer: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone 1–2, and some roles require no prior experience. A portfolio or demonstrable presentation capability is still needed; specifics depend on employer and project requirements.
questions.question: Can I enter without experience?

questions.answer: Investigate agency and direct-client channels. This page has not obtained booking channel shares. Before signing, verify the organization, commissions, duration, and upfront conditions.
questions.question: Must I sign with an agency?

questions.answer: Legitimate agencies charge commissions after you obtain work and do not require payment for opportunities. Verify upfront payment requests first and retain evidence.
questions.question: What if I am asked to pay training or shooting fees first?

questions.answer: Treat suggestions making weight loss a work condition cautiously. Individuals and medical professionals determine health boundaries. France and some other countries require medical examinations and agency licensing for modeling practice; other countries have different rules. Verify local requirements separately.
questions.question: Can I refuse requests to lose weight for work?

questions.answer: First check contractual usage scope, duration, and media. Discuss out-of-scope use with agents and clients and seek local legal channels if needed.
questions.question: What if photographs are reused after a shoot?

questions.answer: Calculate hourly pay and out-of-pocket costs by project, including transportation, makeup and hair, clothing, and time, and retain work orders and payment records. Official wage statistics exclude self-employed workers and cannot be applied directly.
questions.question: How should self-employed models verify income?

questions.answer: This occupation commonly involves prolonged standing, bending, and frequent clothing changes, along with possible weight and appearance pressure. This page provides no medical advice; seek medical care for persistent symptoms.
questions.question: What health requirements does this work involve?

questions.answer: Interview cases document generated materials and digital replicas. Insufficient evidence: actual replacement probabilities by direction and national net job and income outcomes have not been obtained.
questions.question: Will AI-generated images affect my work?

questions.answer: Use O*NET profiles to verify tasks and preparation levels, BLS wages and projections to verify national definitions, and local labor laws and authorities to verify contracts and permission rules.
questions.question: Where can I verify official information?

subject.name: Models
subject.summary: Models (O*NET-SOC 41-9012.00) display clothing and accessories to prospective buyers at fashion shows, private showings, or retail settings, and pose for magazines, advertisements, painting, sculpture, and other art. Work primarily involves agency bookings and projects, with unstable income and schedules. Models must verify contracts, likeness usage scope, and working conditions themselves.
